newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco says union talks at critical stage.
newsitem.headline: Inco says union talks at critical stage.

text.p: Inco Ltd said on Thursday that talks with striking unionized workers at its Sudbury, Ontario nickel mine were at a critical stage.

"We met with the senior negotiators in the company of the provincial government mediator...and I would characterize the discussions (as) at a very critical stage at this point," Inco spokesman Jerry Rodgers told Reuters.

However, a spokesman for Local 6500 of the United Steelworkers of America, representing the 4,670 striking mineworkers, said talks had broken off as a result of new concessions introduced by Inco in a counter-proposal to a union offer delivered through mediator, Dennis Nelson, earlier this week.

"Talks just broke off and the strike continues," said union spokesman Wayne Fraser. "They put a proposal on the table that failed to address three of our major issues and had three new concessions on it. We were outraged, the employees are going to be outraged and I think this community is going to be outraged at their attitude."

Fraser said the provincial mediator left Sudbury and returned to Toronto, but the union would be willing to return to the talks if Inco was willing to discuss an offer from the union before it expires on June 30.
"The ball is in their court again and when they want to resume negotiations (they can) call us," Fraser said. "But I don't think that's going to happen until at least August or maybe September."
Inco's unionized Sudbury workers went on strike at midnight on Monday, June 2, after voting 60.4 percent against a contract offer endorsed by union leaders.
According to Inco's 1997 production plan, the Ontario division was expected to produce about 230 million pounds of nickel, about 200 million pounds of copper and about four million pounds of cobalt.

Inco's Port Colborne, Ontario refinery, which processes cobalt, precious metals and electro-nickel, was not affected by the Sudbury strike. Unionized workers at the Port Colborne refinery approved the contract on Monday, June 2.
